column1: # The directory trees the QA gates must not gate on, one source for both readers:
# scripts/lib/qa-trees.bash (the bash gates, through scripts/qa-discovery.bash), the Go readers
# (src-go/qa/discovery, src-go/qa/patterns) and the Go qa-changed (src-go/qa/changed). A hand edit
# to one reader would be invisible to the others, so there is only this file; src-go/qa/changed
# carries a test that the bash and Go readers agree.
#   list  shell: shell, YAML and JavaScript discovery. python: Python discovery, narrower inside
#         .claude/ccy because claude-supervise.py is tracked and must stay gated.
#   dir   a directory name matched as a whole /<dir>/ segment sequence anywhere in the path,
#         not only at the repository root.
# .git, .ansible: the WHOLE .ansible tree, not just roles/. It is gitignored Galaxy output and
#   `ansible-galaxy collection install` populates .ansible/collections/ with thousands of
#   third-party files carrying their own lint findings. Gating them made QA non-idempotent: a
#   repo that passed the first run failed the second, on vendored upstream fixtures.
# .claude/hooks-daemon-backups: the upgrade keeps the previous copy of any daemon-deployed tree
#   it replaces; it is a byte copy of .claude/skills, already excluded, and is recreated by
#   every upgrade, so deleting the directory defers the failure rather than fixing it.
# .claude/ccy: the whole CCY runtime tree (snapshots, plugins, history) for shell. Python
#   excludes only plugins, file-history and projects (saved transcripts of a Read of a script
#   start with its shebang), because claude-supervise.py is tracked. It is daemon-owned and
#   rewritten on every upgrade; upstream guarantees it clean under ruff's default rules, and a
#   finding from a rule this repo selected is excluded here, not patched (CLAUDE/QA.md).
# .claude/worktrees: checkouts of other branches, gated on their own branch.
# .semgrep: annotated rule FIXTURES, deliberately full of the broken patterns the rules must
#   catch; validated by `semgrep --test` in qa-patterns.bash, which is the check that belongs to it.
